status: draft v0 — derived from the September golden set traps; Head of Product to review

criteria.text: Every part of the message is answered: each question, each ask and each verdict gets a reply; a two-list ask ('Burmese / Japanese') gets both lists; a fork ('museum first or market first') is answered both ways.
pass_examples: The ask had three parts (is this cuisine in the profile, how far is the named place, the best of that cuisine here) and the answer has a line for each.
'No Thai, no Burmese, and no Italian' was read as three exclusions and none of the picks is any of them, with the exclusions named in the header.
fail_examples: The message asked for lunch and dessert; the answer covers lunch only.
A 93-character non-answer ('tell me more about what you want') to a plain 'quick snack near the stay' ask.

criteria.text: The meal or slot is the one asked about, not the clock's; a meal already had is history and is not re-recommended.
pass_examples: 'Had dinner at X, where for dessert?' → dessert picks near X; no dinner places.
'Vegan lunch places tomorrow' → lunch picks checked for tomorrow's lunch hours, not tonight's.
fail_examples: 'Where for dessert' answered with dinner restaurants because it is 7 PM.
'Quick snack' treated as dinner because 'snack' is not a meal word.

criteria.text: The right people: the speaker is identified, the diners are who the message says (the spouse only, the two adults, a guest), and a guest with unknown rules is handled as such.
pass_examples: 'I'm the wife, meeting friends' → speaker spouse, diners spouse + friends; the friends' rules unknown and said so.
'Lunch for my wife only' → one diner line, the spouse's.
fail_examples: 'For my wife' answered with a line for the primary member's dish too.
A friend joining the day is ignored: no line, no note.

criteria.text: The right place: where they are versus where to look versus a route; a landmark or dictated name is resolved; a negated place is excluded; an ambiguous place is read sensibly and said so.
pass_examples: 'Walking to the river from the stay' read as origin = the stay, route = the river path, with the ambiguity named in one line.
A dictated 'veggie delight' resolved to the known 'Veggie Galaxy' from the last answer.
fail_examples: 'Closer to the neighborhood' ignored; picks across town.
'Where are you?' asked back to someone who just named their origin.

criteria.text: The right time: now, later or tomorrow; departure plus travel = arrival; 'open by 6:30'; a deadline at the destination; hours judged at that time.
pass_examples: 'We'd start for dinner at 7:15' → hours checked for about 7:35 arrival.
'Coffee open by 6:30 tomorrow' → tomorrow 6:30 is the check time.
fail_examples: Hours checked at 6:40 PM for a 7:35 arrival.
A museum that closes at 5 ignored in a 'before the museum' ask at 2 PM.

criteria.text: Continuity: a correction or plan edit inherits everything it does not change (diners, overrides, the time, the area); a rejected pick never returns; a 'something else' is new places.
pass_examples: 'I will be starting from the stay' after a coffee ask keeps coffee, tomorrow and 6:30 and only changes the origin.
After 'these are boring', none of the earlier picks appear again.
fail_examples: The same answer served again to a reworded follow-up.
A diet override from twenty minutes earlier is dropped in the follow-up.

criteria.text: Inferences are stated in one line each; at most one question; a fork is answered both ways rather than asked about.
pass_examples: 'Assuming the baby is along.' stated once at the top.
An ambiguous area resolved with a one-line 'reading X as Y' instead of a question.
fail_examples: Two questions before any pick.
An assumption about who is eating made silently.

criteria.text: The room suits an infant: calm, stroller room, earlier tables, never a bar; no outdoor-only seating in rain or cold; the answer says what it knows about the room.
pass_examples: A dining room with highchairs and an early table suggested, with the source of the room note.
A counter-only place left out with 'no stroller room' as the reason.
fail_examples: A late 9 PM table with the baby and no mention of it.
A patio-only place under a wind warning.

criteria.text: The coffee ritual: a local roaster's espresso with a gluten-free pastry for the primary member, or an honest 'coffee only here'.
pass_examples: A roaster with a GF pastry named, and the alternative with coffee only labeled as such.
'Coffee only for the primary member here; the GF pastry is at the bakery two blocks on.'
fail_examples: A chain café as the pick with no roaster considered.
A pastry named for the primary member with no word on whether it is gluten-free.

criteria.text: Weather: the newest official forecast with its issuance time is used; active hazards change the plan (indoors, off the waterfront, the order of stops).
pass_examples: 'NWS 7:49 AM: coastal flood warning to 8 PM' quoted and the waterfront stop moved before the rain.
A storm plan offered with the original order as the alternative.
fail_examples: A day plan under a high wind warning with no mention of weather.
Yesterday's forecast used for tomorrow's plan.

criteria.text: No false none: a 'nothing fits' names the area and hour searched and offers the nearest place that qualifies.
pass_examples: 'Nothing in that town fits by 6:30; the nearest that does is 9 minutes away.'
'No Korean within the drive budget on the lists I checked; the nearest is X.'
fail_examples: 'There is no good Korean food around here' in a city known for it, with no list named.
A none with no nearest alternative.

criteria.text: Favorites first: each member's favorite cuisines and the household's saved places lead when the ask allows; a save that fits is named or its omission explained.
pass_examples: The household's saved place for this cuisine is the first pick.
A favorite cuisine leads the list on an open 'match our profile' ask.
fail_examples: A saved pasta place with a GF menu never shown in a pasta ask.
Favorites ignored on an open ask.

criteria.text: A signature dish for each diner, inside their rules; substitutions named ('without the dried shrimp', 'a cup, not the cone').
pass_examples: The tea leaf salad for the spouse without the dried shrimp; the house noodle for the primary member with the GF noodle.
Ice cream in a cup for the primary member unless the cone is gluten-free.
fail_examples: 'Something vegetarian' with no dish named.
A beef dish named for a vegetarian diner.

criteria.text: The format matches the ask: quick, hole in the wall, sit down nicely, takeout; a mismatch is said, not hidden.
pass_examples: A counter place for 'quick bites'.
A table-service room for 'sit down nicely' with the room described.
fail_examples: A fine-dining room for 'hole in the wall'.
A takeout-only place for a sit-down ask with no mention of it.

criteria.text: After 'boring': lead with the city's signature inside the rules, with a split order where diners' rules collide; no gate lifted to please.
pass_examples: The city's signature dish for the primary member and a separate order for the spouse, eaten together at the stay.
'Yes, the city is known for X; here is X inside your rules, and why the earlier picks were not it.'
fail_examples: A seafood-led room for the whole table despite the spouse's rule, because 'boring' was said.
The same safe picks again after 'boring'.

criteria.text: The next step where it matters: book, call first, cash only, parking, validation; nothing invented.
pass_examples: 'Cash and one card brand only' flagged from the place's own page.
'Call ahead for the GF injera' when the source says to.
fail_examples: A parking claim with no source.
No 'call first' on a place whose hours could not be confirmed.

criteria.text: Left out, with a short reason each, when a likely candidate was excluded (a chain, a bar, closed today, below the rating floor).
pass_examples: 'Left out: X (a chain), Y (closed Mondays).'
The place the owner named is in 'left out' with why it misses.
fail_examples: An obvious candidate silently missing.
A 'left out' with no reasons.

criteria.text: The day plan covers what is left of the day, including the rhythm slots (coffee, dessert after lunch, gelato after dinner), in a sensible order.
pass_examples: Coffee → the run → breakfast → lunch → coffee at 3 → dinner → gelato, each with a place and a time.
A plan that starts at noon covers lunch through gelato and says the morning is past.
fail_examples: A plan with dinner before lunch.
A full-day plan with no coffee slot for a household that has coffee times.

criteria.text: Weather windows respected in the plan: outdoors before the rain, off the waterfront under a flood warning, the storm's peak indoors.
pass_examples: The river walk moved to the morning before the rain.
The waterfront market dropped under the coastal flood warning, with a reason.
fail_examples: An outdoor market at the storm's peak.
A plan that ignores a wind warning quoted in the ask.

criteria.text: Coverage behind a negative claim: any 'none' or 'nothing fits' names the list or sweep it rests on.
pass_examples: 'On the two critics' lists and the knowledge base, nothing Burmese within 15 minutes.'
'The one Burmese place on the aggregator is the one above; no second one listed.'
fail_examples: 'There is no Burmese here' with nothing named.
A negative claim contradicted by a saved place in the knowledge base.

criteria.text: An exclusion's exception clause ('unless something super cool') is used only with named acclaim and a stated reason.
pass_examples: The excluded cuisine offered once, with the named list that praises it and the reason in one line.
The exception not used; the exclusion honored.
fail_examples: The excluded cuisine offered with 'it's great' and no source.
The exception used for two picks.
